headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang unveils modular AI data centers for Europe
summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announced the DSX Pod, a plug-and-play data center solution designed to be brought online in just 14 days, aiming to accelerate AI adoption across Europe.
details: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang presented his vision for Europe's AI future at the company's global conference in Berlin, focusing on robotics, AI agents, and modular data centers.

The new DSX Pod is a "plug-and-play" modular data center that can be assembled and brought online in 14 days, a significant reduction from the months or years typically required for traditional infrastructure projects.
Huang emphasized that Europe is well-positioned to lead in the emerging "next great industry" of humanoid robotics, leveraging its manufacturing heritage.
Nvidia is also launching a full-stack robotics platform and a reference robot called Agile One, set for release in Q1 next year, to help developers build physical AI systems.
The company announced partnerships with European automakers VW and Mercedes-Benz for autonomous vehicle development, further integrating Nvidia's technology into the automotive sector.
Huang predicted that future companies will utilize a combination of closed and open AI models, with customization on proprietary data being key to achieving frontier performance.
He also highlighted the growing demand for computing power driven by AI agents, which are pushing token consumption and the need for advanced GPUs higher.
caption:
Nvidia's Jensen Huang is bringing "AI factories" to Europe with a new modular data center solution that can be deployed in just 14 days.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang presented his vision for Europe's AI future at the company's global conference in Berlin, focusing on robotics, AI agents, and modular data centers.

The new DSX Pod is a "plug-and-play" modular data center that can be assembled and brought online in 14 days, a significant reduction from the months or years typically required for traditional infrastructure projects.

Huang emphasized that Europe is well-positioned to lead in the emerging "next great industry" of humanoid robotics, leveraging its manufacturing heritage.

Nvidia is also launching a full-stack robotics platform and a reference robot called Agile One, set for release in Q1 next year, to help developers build physical AI systems.

The company announced partnerships with European automakers VW and Mercedes-Benz for autonomous vehicle development, further integrating Nvidia's technology into the automotive sector.

Huang predicted that future companies will utilize a combination of closed and open AI models, with customization on proprietary data being key to achieving frontier performance.

He also highlighted the growing demand for computing power driven by AI agents, which are pushing token consumption and the need for advanced GPUs higher.
